title: M6: replay-from-raw
description:
Turn raw retention into an actual safety net, not a promise.

  - CLI: replay --batch-id=N re-runs the entire pipeline from import_batch.raw_payload
  - import_batch records raw bytes + sha256 + parser version
  - Enables: schema changes that affect normalization, categorization rule changes, and full rebuild
    after any bug in the pipeline

  This is the mitigation for risk #9 (schema churn during vibe-coding destroying real financial
  history) and the answer to the Amex 6-month CSV window, where archived exports are the only
  durable copy of anything.
design: Requires import_batch.raw_payload to never be deleted. That is a P0 invariant from M0, and this milestone is what proves it has teeth.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting every journal_entry and journal_line, then running replay, reproduces the ledger exactly. Changing a category rule and replaying re-categorizes without re-importing the file. Done BEFORE any schema churn, as promised in the roadmap.
close_reason: M6 replay-from-raw shipped: lifeos-cli replay --batch-id re-parses raw_payload with a frozen-fingerprint guard, detaches+deletes orphaned entries, re-books via the existing writer chain, and re-applies DB categorization rules. Acceptance #1 (delete all journal rows, replay reproduces the ledger) and #2 (rule change re-categorizes) verified in test_replay_db.py. Gates green: ruff/format/mypy --strict; non-DB 450 passed; DB 133 passed. Multi-section Revolut replay deferred to a filed follow-up bead.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Implemented. New files: backend/finance/api/replay.py (replay_batch / ReplayReport / ReplayError), backend/finance/ingestion/rules.py (load_rules), backend/cli.py (lifeos-cli replay --batch-id). pyproject.toml gains the lifeos-cli console script. writers.py gains an optional source_record_id that attaches to an existing immutable source_record instead of inserting; the None path is unchanged and every current caller passes None.

DESIGN DECISIONS
- Re-parse from import_batch.raw_payload, not re-book from source_record: the raw file is the input that can cross parser/normalization versions; source_record stays the uniqueness anchor. Fingerprints are recomputed by the same _content_only_ranks/_fingerprint composition and must equal the stored set. Any symmetric difference raises ReplayError BEFORE anything is detached, so no partial rebuild is ever left behind.
- parser_version deliberately NOT added: the fingerprint algorithm is already hash-pinned, the divergence check surfaces parser drift loudly, and no build-time version constant exists. Recorded here rather than silently omitted.
- Categorization is wired into REPLAY ONLY; the import path is unchanged. load_rules projects category_rule rows to the categorize engine dataclass. A matching rule wins over the previous value (else 'change the rule and replay' could never re-categorize); a pre-replay snapshot restores a hand-set category on lines no rule matches. Caveat: a category applied by an earlier replay is indistinguishable from a hand edit, so DELETING a rule leaves its old category behind. Not acceptance-blocking.
- Orphan deletion is bounded to entries this batch pointed at; a global orphan sweep would delete the whole ledger on a batch with no entries.

KNOWN LIMITATION: a multi-section (Revolut) or otherwise partial batch with unattributed rows cannot replay, because section_account_ids is not persisted and those rows have no fingerprint scope; replay raises loudly. Follow-up bead filed (discovered-from this one).

VERIFICATION (independent): ruff check + ruff format --check clean; mypy --strict clean (87 files); non-DB pytest 450 passed / 133 deselected; full DB pytest 133 passed / 450 deselected; test_replay_db.py 4 passed.

title: M4: transfer matching + the Amex card payment
description:
The correctness requirement. Once this works, spending totals are trustworthy.

  - transfer_match table (stored, never recomputed, with match_method + confidence + confirmed_at)
  - Own-account transfers: Rabobank <-> Revolut, excluded from spending
  - THE AMEX CASE: a EUR 50 Amex purchase is an expense on a liability account; a later Rabobank
    -50 'American Express' has NO matching row to link, because the liability balance simply falls.
    Synthesize the liability leg (is_synthesized, synthesized_reason='card_payment') so the entry
    balances and spending is 50 once, never 100.
  - SEPA direct debit vs own-account transfer: deterministic rule, else review queue
  - Nightly sweep for unmatched outbound legs whose other leg has not been imported yet
  - Review queue UX: CONFIRM / REJECT / IGNORE

  Deliberately NOT implemented: Hungarian one-to-one assignment (borrowed from BankingSync). It
  solves batched ambiguous matching, which does not exist at 3 accounts. Reconsider only if the
  review queue shows real ambiguous clusters.
design: Card-payment detection is ILIKE '%american express%' at confidence 0.95 with user rejection allowed, and it LEARNS: after confirmation the observed description is promoted to a rule. Brittle on day one, self-correcting by month three.
acceptance_criteria: THE HEADLINE TEST: Amex 50 purchase then Rabobank -50 -> total spending is 50, not 100. Both journal entries balance. Two EUR 50 transfers the same day produce 2 distinct transfer_match rows, not 1 merged pair. A SEPA DD to a third party is an expense with no transfer_match. An ambiguous DD-vs-transfer lands in the review queue rather than being guessed.
close_reason: M4 transfer matching shipped: own-account linker (import + sweep, shared), transfer_review/transfer_skip + review API (confirm/reject/ignore), lifeos-cli sweep, M6 replay integration with CASCADE fix, and the frontend review queue. All acceptance criteria covered by tests incl. the headline 50-not-100 spending, two distinct same-day matches, third-party DD stays expense, ambiguity queues. Verified: ruff/format/mypy clean (94 files), non-DB 450 passed, DB 155 passed (+22), frontend 73 tests + build. Deferred: description-based DD classifier and the separate absorb_fx_residual posting defect (filed as a follow-up bead).

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
M4 delivered. What was already built and left alone: the transfer_match schema and the Amex card-payment case (ADR 0007) were already implemented and tested; M4 did not touch that writer.

WHAT SHIPPED
- Own-account matching: new finance/api/transfer_linker.py runs the existing PURE rule (domain/services/transfer_match.py, unchanged) from TWO entry points sharing one function — a post-persist call in routes/imports.py, and a nightly-ish sweep. Auto-links only an exact same-currency same-day opposite pair on two different own accounts (match_method auto_amount_date, confidence 0.95, confirmed_at NULL); stamps both lines and sets is_transfer on both entries. Integrity split out of the way: synthesized legs (owned by the card writer) and same-entry legs are excluded.
- Review queue: migration 0004 adds finance.transfer_review and finance.transfer_skip; routes/review.py rewritten from the stub to GET /review/transfers, GET /review/transfers/stats, POST .../{id}/confirm|reject|ignore. Ambiguous cases (multi-candidate, or a lone cross-currency candidate) are queued, never guessed. CONFIRM takes the chosen candidate_journal_line_id; REJECT leaves the ledger untouched; IGNORE writes transfer_skip so the sweep stops re-suggesting.
- Sweep: finance/api/sweep.py + a lifeos-cli sweep subcommand (--from/--to), idempotent. No worker container: PHASE2-PLAN 3c ('delete the worker, re-add with Enable Banking') is reaffirmed; host cron runs the CLI.
- M6 replay integration: replay re-links transfers between re-book and categorize; migration 0004 adds ON DELETE CASCADE to the two transfer_match FKs, fixing a dormant replay FK violation that surfaced the moment a transfer match existed in a replayed batch.

ACCEPTANCE (all in test_transfer_match_db.py unless noted): same-day pair auto-links and is excluded from spending; two same-day pairs produce two distinct matches; a third-party DD stays an expense with no match; two candidates land in the queue; cross-currency never auto-matches; the headline Amex purchase + Rabobank payment totals spending 50 not 100 with both entries balanced; review confirm/reject/ignore + no re-suggest in test_review_queue_db.py; sweep backlog/idempotency/ignore in test_sweep_db.py; replay reproduction in test_replay_with_transfers_db.py; card-payment not re-matched in test_card_payment_db.py.

FRONTEND: review feature rebuilt against the frozen contract (outbound vs candidates, candidate selection, CONFIRM/REJECT/IGNORE, optimistic removal, loading/empty/error states). The designer session errored before reporting, so I verified it myself and fixed one test typo (teruggeve -> teruggave).

KNOWN LIMITS (recorded, not blockers): the matcher is content-only, so a single wrong same-amount same-day candidate on two own accounts still auto-links without appearing in the queue (multi-candidate is caught, a lone wrong one is not); auto-matched pairs are not reviewable after the fact; a description-based DD-vs-transfer classifier is deferred. The broader absorb_fx_residual posting defect is filed separately (discovered-from this bead); M4 only refuses cross-currency auto-matching.

VERIFICATION (mine, after all lanes): ruff + ruff format clean; mypy --strict clean (94 files); non-DB pytest 450 passed; DB pytest 155 passed (was 133, +22); frontend lint clean, 73 tests passed, production build succeeded.

title: M2: Amex CSV import + fingerprint dedup
description:
The milestone that proves correctness, and the only ingestion path guaranteed to exist.

  - SourceAdapter protocol + AmexCsvAdapter (column mapping from the LifeOS-2 findings)
  - import_batch (retains raw_payload, never deleted) + source_record (immutable raw_data)
  - Normalization into journal_entry/journal_line, double-entry
  - Tier 3 fingerprint: SHA256 over canonicalised
    description|amount|currency|date|account_id|occurrence_index
  - occurrence_index via ROW_NUMBER() so two identical EUR 3.20 coffees produce TWO entries
  - The cross-batch UNIQUE index on (fingerprint, account_id)
  - Categorization deferred to M3 - everything lands uncategorized

Note: Amex has NO stable transaction IDs, so Tier 1 is unavailable here. This IS the Tier 3 path.
design: fingerprint.py is a pure function with no I/O so it is exhaustively unit-testable, and it is hash-frozen from the start. Changing it later invalidates every stored fingerprint - that is why it is an invariant.
acceptance_criteria: Import September.csv twice -> second import creates 0 new journal_entry rows; all source_record rows marked status='duplicate'. Two identical EUR 3.20 coffees on the same day -> 2 entries with occurrence_index 1 and 2. Re-import after row reordering -> no duplicates. raw_description is byte-identical after any user edit.
close_reason: Superseded by LifeOS-18: Amex is PDF-only (app offers no CSV), so there is no CSV source. Dedup obligations transferred to LifeOS-12 / M7.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
SUPERSEDED by LifeOS-18 (2026-10-01). The user will download Amex statements as PDF from the mobile app, which offers PDF export only - there is no CSV to import, so this milestone has no source.

Its acceptance criteria are unachievable as written, and notably one of them was the most consequential open item in the whole plan: 'import September.csv twice -> second import creates 0 new journal_entry rows'. title: absorb_fx_residual silently books a real FX loss into the largest leg
description:
Pre-existing defect recorded in docs/PHASE2-PLAN.md 3d, surfaced again by the M4 transfer-matching design review and deliberately NOT fixed in LifeOS-9.

WHAT: backend/finance/domain/services/manual_posting.py absorb_fx_residual() absorbs a multi-currency residual into the largest leg instead of recording it as its own fact, so a real FX gain/loss is silently folded into another line and is invisible in the ledger.

WHY IT MATTERS: CROSS_CURRENCY_TOLERANCE_MINOR = 50 in domain/services/transfer_match.py made a cross-currency pair within 50 minor look like a transfer, which would have hidden a real FX loss as a transfer. LifeOS-9 mitigated the MATCHER path (the transfer linker filters candidates to same-currency only; cross-currency pairs never auto-link and go to the review queue). That does NOT fix the posting defect: any multi-currency posting through build_expense_legs/absorb_fx_residual still hides the residual.

WORK: decide whether to (a) post the FX residual explicitly as its own gain/loss line, or (b) refuse the posting when a residual would be absorbed. Then a test proving a real FX loss is visible rather than absorbed. Acceptance: no posting silently absorbs a non-zero FX residual.

FOUND IN: LifeOS-9 (M4) design review. Related: docs/PHASE2-PLAN.md section 3d, docs/adr/0007.
close_reason: absorb_fx_residual now refuses to absorb a residual larger than the 0.005 balance tolerance, so a real FX gain/loss can no longer be silently folded into a leg. Confirmed the two-leg production path was already an exact no-op (no live loss); the latent 3-leg defect is reproduced and now raises ManualPostingError. The matcher half of PHASE2-PLAN 3d was already closed in LifeOS-9. Verified: ruff/format/mypy clean (94 files), non-DB 450 passed, DB 156 passed (+1).

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Premise checked before fixing, and it is narrower than the bead title suggests — worth recording.

CURRENT STATE: every production caller of absorb_fx_residual passes exactly the two legs from build_expense_legs (writers.default_leg_builder and routes/transactions), and those are exact negations, so the residual is 0 and absorption is an exact no-op today. Reproduced empirically with a USD funding leg at rate 1.10: absorbing changed nothing. So no live FX loss is being hidden in the current two-leg path.

THE REAL DEFECT IS LATENT BUT REAL: the function will silently fold a genuine difference into the largest leg. Reproduced with three legs summing to 1.00 EUR: absorb_fx_residual shifted the largest leg by 1.00 EUR and produced a balanced entry, erasing the difference. That is the behaviour PHASE2-PLAN section 3d warns about, and it becomes live the moment any third leg (an FX fee, a split) is added.

FIX: absorb only a ROUNDING residual. After computing the residual, if the largest leg would have to move by more than BASE_BALANCE_TOLERANCE (0.005, the exact line the balance trigger in migration 0001 uses), raise ManualPostingError and tell the caller to post the difference as its own leg. A residual up to 0.005 is still absorbed, so the existing exactly-0.0050 test still passes and the two-leg no-op is unchanged.

DECISION — refuse, not book: chose 'refuse' over 'book an explicit FX gain/loss leg' because the model has no FX gain/loss account yet; refusing is the minimal honest guarantee and does not invent ledger structure. Booking explicitly remains the option if 3-leg postings are ever introduced.

NOT IN SCOPE, ALREADY DONE: the matcher half of section 3d (CROSS_CURRENCY_TOLERANCE_MINOR = 50 turning a real FX loss into an apparent transfer) was closed in LifeOS-9 — the transfer linker never auto-matches a cross-currency pair.

VERIFICATION: ruff + ruff format clean; mypy --strict clean (94 files); non-DB pytest 450 passed; DB pytest 156 passed (was 155; +1 new test test_a_real_residual_is_refused_not_absorbed, and the existing 0.005 absorption test still passes).

title: Seed a demo ledger: the database is empty, and chart work has no data
description:
Found while writing PRODUCT.md (LifeOS-9zb). Recorded there under Evidence as an absence future work must not fabricate, but nothing tracks the fix.

THE STATE
  - There is no seed script anywhere. `make` has no seed target.
  - `data/extracted/` holds three REAL Amex card extractions: 2026-06-23 and 2026-07-23, plus manifests, parse reports and selftests. Card only, two months.
  - No checking account. No savings. No multi-month history. No income.

WHY THIS BLOCKS WORK THAT IS OTHERWISE READY
The read-side analytics endpoints (LifeOS-5mq) are built and tested: net-worth, spend-by-category, cashflow. DESIGN.md's own rule - do not chart before an aggregation endpoint exists - is now satisfied. But designing a dashboard against an empty database means designing against an assumption.

  - An empty-state-first design is possible but is not the hard case. The hard case is a user with eleven months of history, four accounts, one of which is a card in a different currency.
  - Charts fail at the edges: a category with one transaction, a month with no spending, a net-worth line that goes flat for nine months then jumps. None of those appear in three card statements.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT BE
Not a mock. Not invented numbers presented as real. A demo ledger is legitimate precisely because it is labelled a demo - the failure mode to avoid is a screenshot or a test fixture that gets mistaken for a user's actual position. Name it, and keep real statement data out of it.

SUGGESTED SHAPE
A script that posts a synthetic-but-argued ledger through the same service layer real imports use, so the analytics queries are exercised by the same code path: several accounts across natures (checking, savings, card, an investment holding), income, recurring spending, transfers between own accounts, a card payment, and deliberately awkward edges (a single-transaction category, an empty month, an FX purchase). Plus a Makefile target.

title: M6 replay cannot rebuild a multi-section batch (section_account_ids not persisted)
description:
Found while implementing LifeOS-11 (M6: replay-from-raw).

WHAT: replay_batch() re-parses a batch from import_batch.raw_payload and requires the re-parsed rows' fingerprints to match the stored source_record fingerprints exactly. A row whose account_id is None (an unattributed row) has no fingerprint scope and is refused, so any batch containing one cannot be replayed.

WHO IT HITS: a Revolut annual statement carries an Account section and a Deposit section. import_batch does not persist the section->account mapping (section_account_ids), so the import route constructs RevolutPdfAdapter() with no mapping; Deposit rows come back account_id=None and are never stored. Re-parsing on replay therefore produces rows the stored set cannot contain, and replay raises 'line N names no account' instead of reproducing the stored subset. The verified Rabobank/Amex single-account batches replay correctly.

WHY DEFERRED, NOT A BUG: the architecture review for M6 accepted this as a loud divergence (documented in finance/api/replay.py) rather than a partial apply. It is a real functional gap for the second multi-section provider.

OPTIONS: (a) persist section_account_ids (or the per-section account ids actually used) on import_batch at upload, and read them back on replay; or (b) change replay's divergence check to compare only attributable rows against the stored set and report unattributed rows the way the import counted them. (a) is the honest fix because the import is what dropped the rows; (b) alone would replay a lossy subset silently. Acceptance: a Revolut batch with a mapped Deposit section replays to the same journal facts as its import.

VERIFY: needs the real Revolut statement and an account mapping for both sections.

title: Analytics: decide whether hidden or closed accounts count toward totals
description:
Found while building the analytics endpoints (LifeOS-6cy). Deliberately unresolved rather than guessed.

GET /api/v1/analytics/{net-worth,spend-by-category,cashflow} currently ignore BOTH account.is_active and account.is_hidden. They are not filtered either way, and the route docstring says why, but the question is genuinely open:

  is_hidden  - does it mean 'do not list this account in the UI' or 'do not count it in my totals'? The column name reads as the first. If a user hides a joint account they still jointly own, the second reading silently removes money from their net worth, and nothing on the page would say so.
  is_active  - a closed account still held a balance on the day it closed. Dropping it rewrites history; keeping it means a long-closed savings account sits in every total forever.

Both defaults currently favour INCLUDING the account, because omitting money from someone's net worth is the worse failure and is invisible, whereas an extra account is visible and looks deliberate.

Needs a product decision, then a test that pins it so a later change is deliberate rather than accidental. Until then this is the most likely way these endpoints report a wrong number without failing anything.
notes: RELATED (2026-10-05): PRODUCT.md records that V1 scope is spending, and savings/investments/net-worth are wanted later. So the decision here should be read with that in mind: whatever is chosen for is_hidden should not make a future investments view impossible to build. Still an open product decision, not a default.

Analytics docstring states the decision (is_hidden is display-only; a closed account still counts on its open dates); 6 db tests pin it across net-worth/spend-by-category/cashflow. title: Analytics: db-marked tests for the net-worth sign rules
description:
The read-side endpoints landed 2026-10-03: GET /api/v1/analytics/{net-worth,spend-by-category,cashflow}, backed by finance/domain/services/analytics.py (pure logic, 25 unit tests) and finance/api/routes/analytics.py (SQL).

WHAT IS UNTESTED, and why it matters more than the rest:
The two rules that decide whether these numbers are truthful live in the SQL and need a real Postgres. They are:

  1. EQUITY IS EXCLUDED from net worth. Spending is parked in a seeded equity contra-account (manual_posting.py). Counting it makes every purchase RAISE the figure it should lower.
  2. LIABILITIES ARE NOT SUBTRACTED. They are already stored negative - a card charge writes a negative line so it balances against the positive equity line. Subtracting the column again reports money you owe as money you have.

Both currently rest on code review and on arithmetic written out in the route docstring. Neither has a test that would catch a regression. A wrong sign here does not raise: it returns a plausible number that disagrees with the user's bank statement.

Build a throwaway lifeos_test database (make up-db, then make test-db) and write db-marked tests that post a small hand-built ledger and assert:
  - a liability charge DECREASES net worth (not increases)
  - equity-only movement does not move net worth
  - an asset-to-asset transfer leaves net worth unchanged
  - a transfer does NOT appear in spend-by-category
  - a transfer DOES appear in cashflow as an asset outflow
  - amounts come back as integer EUR cents, never a float

Also unresolved and worth deciding there: the endpoints ignore account.is_active and account.is_hidden. 'Hidden' may mean 'do not list this account' or 'do not count it in totals' - guessing wrong means money quietly missing from a net worth figure. Needs a product decision, recorded in the route docstring either way.

THE TESTS EARNED THEIR KEEP: they found two real bugs in the queries, both invisible to unit tests. (1) spend-by-category summed BOTH legs of every entry - a two-leg entry carries the category on each side, so every category summed to exactly 0 and every chart bar would have been empty. Fixed by excluding equity accounts, the same exclusion net worth already had. (2) cashflow split movements line-by-line on sign, so the credit leg of a savings top-up read as income - tidying your savings raised your income. Fixed by aggregating per entry and dropping any entry whose every leg is an asset, while keeping transfers that reach a liability so paying a credit card still reads as cash leaving. Ran against a dedicated Postgres on port 55433 rather than the shared test database, which conftest force-drops (WITH FORCE) on every session - running concurrently would have destroyed another agent's database mid-run. title: Counter-leg resolves by exact account name, so renaming the account breaks every manual transaction
description:
Found while reviewing beads on 2026-10-03. Untracked until now.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. POST a manual transaction with no explicit counter_account_id. routes/transactions.py:206 takes the default branch.
2. resolve_default_counter_account() matches account.name == SYSTEM_EXPENSE_ACCOUNT_NAME exactly and case-sensitively (manual_posting.py:245).
3. Rename that account in the UI. Every subsequent manual transaction without an explicit counter_account_id now fails with CounterAccountUnresolvedError: 'No account named ... exists, so there is nowhere to book the other side'.

WHY IT IS WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY INCONVENIENT: the account is looked up by a HUMAN-EDITABLE LABEL to find a row that has a stable primary key. The name is not an identity. The error message says 'create exactly one account with this name', which trains the user toward the fix that makes it worse: creating a SECOND account to restore the magic string, rather than renaming the existing one.

The resolver is otherwise careful -- it distinguishes 'no such account' from 'exists but deactivated', and refuses to pick when two accounts share a name because that would be a coin flip deciding where money goes. The name-based lookup is the one part that treats a label as an identity.

## Options

a) Resolve by id, and treat the name lookup as a last-resort bootstrap only. Cheapest correct fix: the account's primary key is what callers should be sending, and routes/transactions.py:207 already prefers an explicit id when given.
b) Introduce a role/kind column (e.g. system_expense) on account and resolve by that. More correct, and the schema already carries account_nature ('equity'), so this may be smaller than it sounds.
c) Leave it. Defensible ONLY if the name is guaranteed immutable in the UI. Worth checking first: if account names are already unrenameable, this is unreachable and should be closed as such rather than left ambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Renaming the counter-leg account does not break manual transaction posting.
- Whichever option is chosen, there is a test that renames the account and then posts, so the guarantee is enforced rather than assumed.
- If option (c), the unrenameability constraint is asserted in the UI or API layer, and this bead closes with that finding recorded.
close_reason: Done and merged to main (c07e87c). The default contra-leg is resolved by ROLE, not by a human-editable name: account.system_role exists and SYSTEM_EXPENSE_ACCOUNT_ROLE replaces SYSTEM_EXPENSE_ACCOUNT_NAME as the lookup key. Renaming the expense account therefore no longer breaks manual transaction posting, which was the reported failure. The exact-match discipline is kept - it still raises rather than falling back when the role is missing or ambiguous, it just no longer depends on a label the user can edit.

title: generate_types.py emits no real TypeScript types
description:
FOUND DURING M1 (bead LifeOS-6). ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 has been corrected to say codegen is UNIMPLEMENTED rather than claiming CI enforces it.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY: scripts/generate_types.py httpx's http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json and,
on failure, writes a hardcoded 6-line skeleton exporting 'interface LifeOSAppConfig'. It never
emits a single real type. The README's stated commands ('npm run generate:types',
'npx tsx scripts/generate_types.py') do not exist in package.json. frontend/src/api/generated/
is a placeholder README, and the frontend API layer (src/lib/apiClient.ts) is hand-written fetch
plus zod.

WHY IT MATTERS: a change to a Pydantic contract is NOT caught by CI. A zod schema that
disagrees with the server rejects the ENTIRE response array rather than one field, so the
failure surfaces as an empty page with no diagnostic pointing at the schema.

DONE IN M1 (bead LifeOS-6): the four frontend zod id schemas were corrected from
z.string() to z.number().int() when ledger ids became int -- the first real instance of this
class of bug, caught by hand rather than by a gate.

Decide whether to implement real OpenAPI codegen or to state plainly that types are
hand-maintained and add a CI check that the spec and the zod schemas agree.
close_reason: Moot: scripts/generate_types.py was DELETED in commit 8bdfd57. The script that 'emits no real TypeScript types' no longer exists. DECISION RECORD so this is not relitigated: we accept hand-maintained types and build NO OpenAPI codegen and NO zod-vs-spec CI gate. Rationale is the ponytail ladder -- for a single-user app with a 2,754-line frontend, neither the codegen nor the diff gate is a dependency of anything we need. The underlying risk (a hand-written zod schema disagreeing with a Pydantic contract rejects the whole response array, surfacing as an empty page) is ACCEPTED and stays unmitigated until a contract change actually breaks. First real instance of that bug, the id schemas corrected from z.string() to z.number().int() in M1, was caught by hand.

title: Privilege layer: separate app role; GRANTs do not enforce no_cross_schema_fk
description:
DEFERRED OUT OF M1 (bead LifeOS-6) -- a deployment change, not a schema change. Two related gaps, both verified by oracle against a live PostgreSQL 17.11.

1. raw_data_immutable CANNOT be fully enforced by a trigger.
   A BEFORE UPDATE row trigger cannot distinguish 'the statement never mentioned raw_data'
   from 'the statement assigned it its current value'. VERIFIED: an identical-value write
   (UPDATE source_record SET raw_data = raw_data) sails through the M1 trigger.
   The mechanism that does reject it is column privilege:
       REVOKE UPDATE ON source_record FROM lifeos_app;
       GRANT UPDATE (status, journal_entry_id, error_message, occurrence_index) TO lifeos_app;
   IMPORTANT AND EASY TO GET WRONG: 'REVOKE UPDATE (raw_data, raw_description)' ALONE IS A
   SILENT NO-OP while the role still holds table-level UPDATE. Verified -- information_schema
   still showed UPDATE on raw_data after the column revoke, and the write went through.
   Table-level revoke is mandatory.
   Operational hazard to document: because the GRANT enumerates allowed columns, any column
   added later without updating it silently becomes un-updatable. That is a loud failure
   (permission denied), which is the right direction.

2. no_cross_schema_fk is enforced ONLY by the regex in invariants.yaml.
   ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 previously credited 'Postgres grants/role setup' as the DB-level
   half. THAT IS FALSE. The bootstrap does GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA core TO lifeos and
   GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA finance TO lifeos -- a role owning BOTH schemas can create a
   cross-schema foreign key freely. ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 has been corrected.
   A real DB-level enforcement needs a role that does not hold USAGE on the other schema.

M1 SHIPS THE TRIGGER, WHICH BLOCKS EVERY ACTUAL TAMPER (verified, including under superuser).
Only the identical-value write passes, and it changes no data. Hence deferral rather than
silent omission. Rationale: docs/adr/0006-balance-trigger-and-db-invariants.md.
close_reason: no_cross_schema_fk is now DB-enforced by the trg_no_cross_schema_fk ddl_command_end event trigger installed by backend/db_bootstrap.sql (in the DDL's own transaction, superuser included). The bead's 'regex in invariants.yaml' premise was stale: that checker was deleted in 8bdfd57, so the invariant had been enforced by nothing. Docs (ARCHITECTURE §4/§5, ADR 0005/0006) corrected. Verified: ruff/format/mypy clean (100 files), 463 non-DB, 163 DB, 4 new tests ran; migrations still apply with the trigger active.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
SCOPE NARROWED 2026-10-03. Read this bead as the CROSS-SCHEMA FK enforcement work only.

The raw_data_immutable half of this bead -- the identical-value write gap and the
column-privilege layer -- now has its own bead, LifeOS-2h0, which carries the
verified REVOKE trap and the operational hazard in more detail.

The owner explicitly BACKLOGGED the identical-value gap on 2026-10-03 (see
LifeOS-2h0): a same-value write mutates nothing, every actual tamper is already
blocked including under superuser, and the full fix is a deployment change worth
nothing in a single-user app.

WHAT REMAINS HERE: make no_cross_schema_fk actually enforced by the database
rather than by the regex in invariants.yaml. The bootstrap does GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA
core TO lifeos AND GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA finance TO lifeos, so a role owning BOTH
schemas can create a cross-schema foreign key freely. ARCHITECTURE.md section 4
credited grants with enforcing this; that was false and has been corrected.
A real enforcement needs a role that does not hold USAGE on the other schema.

comments.author: LaurenKane
comments.text:
Done. no_cross_schema_fk is now enforced by the DATABASE.

STALE PREMISE, surfaced: the bead said the invariant was enforced "only by the regex in invariants.yaml". That regex — and its whole static checker (scripts/check_invariants.py + invariants.yaml) — was deleted in commit 8bdfd57 ("chore: delete dead code and process scaffolding"), which is in this branch. So the invariant has been enforced by NOTHING since then; ARCHITECTURE.md §4 already said as much. The deliverable is therefore to introduce enforcement where there was none, which is what landed.

MECHANISM: a ddl_command_end event trigger (trg_no_cross_schema_fk + public.fn_no_cross_schema_fk), installed by backend/db_bootstrap.sql (the single source of truth, run by both the postgres entrypoint and the test fixture). It runs inside the DDL's own transaction and RAISEs before commit, so a cross-schema FK can never land — for inline CREATE TABLE and for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT.

WHY AN EVENT TRIGGER AND NOT THE ROLE SEPARATION THE BEAD SUGGESTED: the app/migration/test role lifeos is a PostgreSQL SUPERUSER (verified live: rolsuper=t, rolbypassrls=t). A superuser bypasses USAGE/GRANT checks, so "a role that does not hold USAGE on the other schema" binds nobody in this deployment. Role separation would require a non-superuser per-schema DDL role and a refactor of the migration runner; recommended instead as future hardening (filed as its own bead). The event trigger binds the actual role and is the smallest change that makes the database refuse.

DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED DESIGN (forced, verified): the design's RAISE with %-format args cannot ship in this file. The test fixture executes the whole bootstrap through a parameterized driver (exec_driver_sql), where a bare percent sign reads as a query placeholder and aborts the bootstrap; the docker entrypoint runs the same file through psql, where percent is literal and doubling it would corrupt that path. The trigger raises via RAISE insufficient_privilege USING MESSAGE = <concatenation> instead: same 42501 code, byte-identical text, valid under both callers.

DOCS CORRECTED to match reality: ARCHITECTURE.md §4 (lead-in + the schema-ownership row now names the trigger; Since=LifeOS-ceu) and §5; ADR 0005 (the Context regex quote and the "the regex is the enforcement" bullet now tell the accurate story); ADR 0006 §5 (regex -> trigger).

VERIFICATION (mine, independent): ruff check / ruff format --check / mypy --strict on backend tools all clean (100 files); non-DB pytest 463 passed; DB pytest 163 passed (159 + 4). The real migrations still apply cleanly WITH the trigger active (it is installed before migrations run), so it does not block legitimate DDL. The 4 new tests RAN (none skipped): inline CREATE refused, ALTER TABLE refused, same-schema FK still succeeds (no over-blocking), and the trigger is present in pg_event_trigger. A live proof as the lifeos superuser reproduced `no_cross_schema_fk: finance.<probe> has 1 cross-schema FK(s); refusing` (sqlstate 42501) with no probe artifacts left behind.

RESIDUAL RISK, documented rather than hidden: a superuser can DROP EVENT TRIGGER, so this binds cooperating writers, not an attacker holding the role; and SET session_replication_role = replica skips event triggers (the same Postgres-wide limitation the balance trigger carries). Both are deliberate acts visible in the session.

title: check_invariants.py scans __pycache__/*.pyc and matches prose
description:
FOUND TWICE during M1 (bead LifeOS-6), independently, by two lanes.

scripts/check_invariants.py:iter_source_files walks backend/ with rglob('*') and exclude_globs covers only '**/alembic/versions/*.py.orig'. On this machine 68 .pyc files sit inside the invariant scan.

TWO COMPOUNDING PROBLEMS:
1. check_forbid_regex regex-matches raw file TEXT with no awareness of language. A Python
   docstring or comment that happens to contain a forbidden phrase is reported as a violation.
   Both M1 lanes were caught by this: one wrote a docstring explaining why qualified FK
   targets are banned, using the banned spelling, and it failed check-invariants AND
   invariant-negative.
2. Because .pyc files are scanned, a STALE bytecode file can carry text that no longer
   exists in any .py -- so the checker's verdict depends on whether __pycache__ exists.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR CI, NOT JUST LOCAL: 'make ci' runs 'test' before 'check-invariants',
so .pyc files WILL exist when the checker runs in CI. The gate's result is then a function
of build state rather than of source.

SUGGESTED FIX: add '__pycache__/**' (and '*.pyc') to exclude_globs for the forbid_regex
invariants. This is a false-positive fix and weakens no rule.

Not fixed in M1 deliberately: invariants.yaml is the project's policy file and narrowing
what it scans is a decision for the owner, not something an implementation lane should do
unilaterally.
close_reason: Moot: scripts/check_invariants.py and invariants.yaml were DELETED in commit 8bdfd57 (chore: delete dead code and process scaffolding). The .pyc-scanning false positive cannot recur because the checker that scanned them no longer exists.

title: Ratify or replace the 16 mypy explicit-any ignores (pydantic v2 incompatibility)
description:
Raised while verifying M0 (bead LifeOS-5). Currently UNRATIFIED - the orchestrator's call, needs the user's decision.

THE PROBLEM: pyproject.toml sets both mypy strict=true and disallow_any_explicit=true. That second setting is fundamentally unsatisfiable against pydantic v2. mypy's semanal check runs on the BASE CLASS EXPRESSION, and pydantic's BaseModel.__init__(self, /, **data: Any) trips it for every model - regardless of how our own fields are annotated. So every BaseModel subclass in the project produces an explicit-any error it cannot avoid.

CURRENT RESOLUTION: 16 targeted '# type: ignore[explicit-any]' comments on pydantic model class lines only. The global setting is untouched. Verified the ignores do NOT mask real Any: injecting a deliberate 'APP_ID: Any = None' in config.py is still reported by mypy. Ruff, mypy --strict and the 6 import-linter contracts all pass with this in place.

OPTIONS
  a) Keep the 16 targeted ignores. Precise, local, self-documenting at each site.
     Cost: 16 comment lines that need maintaining if models are added.
  b) Per-module disallow_any_explicit = false override for the four pydantic
     modules. Fewer comments, but a real weakening and it is invisible at the
     call site - a genuine Any in those modules would stop being caught.
  c) Drop disallow_any_explicit globally. Simplest, but loses the check
     everywhere, including the non-pydantic code where it works fine today.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), already in place. This bead exists to record that the
decision was made deliberately rather than by accident, and to revisit if the
model count grows enough for 16 ignores to become noise.

NOTE: no code change required unless you pick (b) or (c).
close_reason: RATIFIED option (a): keep the 16 targeted '# type: ignore[explicit-any]' comments on pydantic model class lines. mypy's disallow_any_explicit is unsatisfiable against pydantic v2 because semanal checks the BASE CLASS expression and BaseModel.__init__(self, /, **data: Any) trips it for every model regardless of field annotations, so the targeted ignores are precise, local and self-documenting; a deliberate 'APP_ID: Any = None' in config.py is still reported by mypy. Global setting untouched, no code change. Confirmed with owner 2026-10-06. Revisit if the model count grows enough for 16 ignores to become noise.

With neither the C extension nor a bundled libpq, every DB operation fails at first use with:

P3 worked around it by installing libpq5 in backend/Dockerfile, so the container is fine. But 'uv sync' on a bare developer host still hits this, which means a fresh clone is not immediately usable for DB work outside Docker.

OPTIONS

     wheels carry their own copy of the client library.
  b) keep bare psycopg and require system libpq - more explicit and matches the
     Netcup VPS target from docs/adr/0001-deployment-topology.md, but every new
     machine needs libpq-dev/libpq5 installed first.
  c) psycopg[c] - build against the system library, for distros that prefer it.

This matters for the project promise of Docker-first deployment, but the developer
experience on a bare host is currently a trap.

DECIDE deliberately and record the choice. Not blocking M0 - the container path
works. Worth settling before M1 (bead LifeOS-6) needs real migrations.

title: Add the Rabobank transaction type-code enum, sourced from the printed legend
description:
Rabobank rows carry a two-letter type code (Value date | Type | Counterparty account | Name/description | Debit amount | Credit amount). The last page of every statement prints a 24-entry legend. No enum for these codes exists anywhere in the repo.

Codes observed in the four supplied statements: ba, bg, bv, cb, db, ei, ga, id, sb, tb, we - all defined by the printed legend, no undefined codes. These matter because they carry meaning the description does not: 'ei' is a Euro direct debit and is how the American Express card payment arrives, 'tb' is an internal account transfer, 'sb' is salary.

One caveat: the 'we' entry is truncated in the source itself, reading 'we = Wero (co branded', so it cannot be resolved further. tools/bankparse/rabo.py parses the legend at runtime rather than hardcoding it.
acceptance_criteria: The type codes are enumerated in the design docs with their printed meanings, the truncation of 'we' is noted, and any consumer treats an unknown code as a parse warning rather than failing or guessing.

title: Decide how to represent the Revolut Deposit-to-IBAN mapping, which the statement does not state
description:
One Revolut statement covers two products, Account (Current Account) with 340 rows and Deposit with 11 rows, and lists two own IBANs: NL69REVO...1997 and LT5032500...9880. The statement never says which IBAN the Deposit product belongs to.

The parser currently attributes Deposit rows to the LT IBAN by inference and flags it as inferred in data/extracted/*_manifest.json. That inference is not in any doc, and an unrecorded guess baked into an import is exactly the kind of thing that becomes load-bearing by accident.

Related: import_batch has a single nullable account_id (ARCH:287) and source_record a single non-null one (ARCH:304), but this file needs two. See docs/research/11 section 3.6.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on whether the Deposit product becomes its own account, a distinct source_record status, or an explicitly inferred account_ref that surfaces for user confirmation. The inference is no longer undocumented.

title: Record the statement-balance identity as a per-account-type import invariant
description:
A current account satisfies: previous + credits - debits = closing. An Amex card satisfies: Vorig + Debiteringen - Crediteringen = Nieuw, i.e. a charge INCREASES the amount owed. Both were verified with zero delta against every supplied statement. A single generic balance self-check cannot be written for both; the identity is per account type.

No source_record or journal_line column stores a statement balance (docs/research/11 section 4 notes this under P-NO-HISTORIC-BALANCE), so the invariant is currently asserted nowhere in the design.

This invariant is what caught every parsing bug during the real-export verification: an off-by-one that mis-attached the Amex CR credit marker, a missing close-column anchor in Revolut, and a wrong sign on the Amex balance identity. It is the cheapest completeness check available and should be a required acceptance test for every new adapter.
acceptance_criteria: ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md defines the per-account-type balance identity and lists balance continuity as an acceptance criterion for every adapter. Documented as an invariant alongside the existing invariants.yaml entries.

title: M5: Enable Banking ingestion for Rabobank
description:
- RS256 JWT client (NOT HS256 - a correction to the original assumption), hand-rolled, no SDK
  - Consent flow: POST /auth -> bank redirect -> POST /sessions
  - Account linking on identification_hash, NEVER on account.uid (uid rotates at every re-auth)
  - Aggressive backfill at consent time with strategy=longest (history clamps to ~90 days shortly
    after consent, so waiting loses data permanently)
  - Polled sync - Enable Banking has NO AIS webhooks. Respect ~4 background fetches/day/ASPSP
    unless PSU headers are supplied.
  - Tier 1 dedup (entry_reference, scoped by account) + Tier 2 pending->booked
  - EXPIRED_SESSION (401) handled as a NORMAL expected re-auth flow, not an error state
  - session_ended_reason recorded as an explicit column

  entry_reference usually only materialises on BOOK, so Tier 2 cannot lean on provider IDs and must
  be confidence-scored with a review queue. Tier 3 fingerprint is computed for API rows too as a
  backstop if entry_reference ever changes on a historical re-fetch.
design: The RSA private key lives in the OS keyring, never the database. Enable Banking issues us no access or refresh tokens - the credential surface is one long-lived key.
acceptance_criteria: Rabobank consent completes end to end. A re-sync of the same window creates 0 duplicates. A PDNG->BOOK transition reconciles into ONE journal_entry, updated in place, preserving any user-set category. EXPIRED_SESSION produces a clear re-auth prompt, not a stack trace. A 90-day backfill lands in full on first consent.

title: M3: merchant normalization + 7-layer categorization
description:
Layer 1 exact user rules / 2 merchant_alias normalization / 3 known NL merchant map /
4 trigram fuzzy / 5 LEARNED FROM MANUAL CORRECTIONS / 6 LLM fallback (opt-in, deferred) /
7 uncategorized review queue.

Layer 5 is the differentiator: NEITHER reference project implements it. Firefly has no evidence of
learnability; Actual has no auto-suggest. Every manual correction raises merchant_alias.confidence to
1.0 or creates an is_learned category_rule, so the queue drains itself.

Rules must stay hand-editable: description_pattern + priority + is_learned. No generic rules DSL,
no YAML logic engine, no expression evaluator. The whole rule set should fit on one screen.
design: Reuse the merchant_alias learning mechanism for card-payment description patterns later rather than inventing a second learning store.
acceptance_criteria: Correcting 'PayPal XYZ' to Entertainment > Music means the NEXT identical transaction categorizes automatically with no hand-authored rule. The uncategorized queue is served by the idx_jl_uncat partial index. Rules are editable in the UI and readable as plain text.
notes:
PRODUCT.md CORRECTION (2026-10-05). This bead said categorisation must stay rule-based and inspectable, which reads as a refusal of automatic categorisation. Confirmed with the owner: automatic categorisation is ACCEPTED. The constraint is only that the user can always override it. Layer 5 (learned from manual corrections) is therefore wanted, not merely tolerated.

SECOND GAP, now in scope: the user can create CUSTOM categories. This bead never mentioned it. POST /api/v1/categories already exists (backend/finance/api/routes/categories.py:30) and Category is a self-referencing tree with a kind column, so the data model supports it - but nothing tests that a user-created category works end to end, and there is no UI to create one.

Do not read PRODUCT.md's 'no opaque categorisation' as a ban on automation. It is a ban on automation the user cannot inspect or override.

title: Product decisions that are wanted but not yet decided: cloud sync, investments, live ingestion
description:
Written after PRODUCT.md (LifeOS-9zb) corrected three scope questions that had been recorded as refusals. Each was confirmed with the owner on 2026-10-05. None of them is a decision to make yet - they are decisions to reach WHEN the preceding work makes them unavoidable. Filing them separately so none is silently dropped, and so no future agent reads a refusal that is not one.

PRODUCT.md, explicitly undecided:
  1. Cloud sync. WANTED eventually. ADR 0001 (Netcup VPS + Tailscale, self-hosted) is the V1 answer and a sync product would supersede it. No work now.
  2. Savings and investment tracking. WANTED after V1. Blocked on LifeOS-l3j (exchange_rate is empty, so a non-EUR holding cannot post at all). V1 scope is spending.
  3. Automatic transaction creation. WANTED, conditional on both Rabobank and Revolut proving linkable through Enable Banking. Beads LifeOS-17 (go/no-go probe) and LifeOS-10 / LifeOS-13 (implementation).

WHAT GENUINELY IS A REFUSAL, for contrast
Single-user. No sharing, no permissions, no second user. That one should not appear on this list and should not be quietly relaxed because cloud sync seems convenient - sync is one user's data in two places, sharing is two users in one ledger.

WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT JUST A PARAGRAPH
Because the failure mode already happened once. These three were originally written into LifeOS-9zb as things LifeOS 'deliberately does not do', which is a claim that future rounds will act on. They were all three wrong, and only asking surfaced it. A decision that is merely undecided is not a decision, and the beads board is where undecided things are visible.

Accept when: all three are either decided with a recorded ADR, or explicitly deferred with a date and the condition that would revisit them.

title: Write PRODUCT.md (durable product context)
description:
The repo has no PRODUCT.md. ARCHITECTURE.md is engineering contract, not product context: it does not say who this is for, what the product refuses to do, or what success looks like.

Why it matters now: the visual world is captured in DESIGN.md (added 2026-10-03, north star 'The Confluence'), but that is strictly visual. Product truth currently lives only in code comments and in the beads board, which is not a durable place to find it.

Impeccable requires PRODUCT.md before init/shape and before any new-surface or replacement visual world. Without it, any future surface work has to re-derive intent from scratch, and there is no record of which constraints are deliberate.

Suggested content: who LifeOS is for (single user, personal finance, NL/EUR-first given Rabobank + Revolut + Amex + Enable Banking); the double-entry-ledger-first philosophy; the offline / no-telemetry guarantee (ARCHITECTURE.md §183, --network=none) as a product constraint not just a test; what it deliberately does not do (no multi-user, no cloud sync, no ML categorisation); and the M1-M10 scope boundary.

Do not duplicate ARCHITECTURE.md. Product truth explains why the product is shaped this way; ARCHITECTURE.md explains how it is built.
close_reason: Done (commit e57088b on the docs branch). PRODUCT.md records the durable product truth that ARCHITECTURE.md deliberately does not: who the product is for, the job it does, and what success looks like. The job is answering any question about one's own money across accounts that bank apps treat as unrelated worlds. The differentiator is stated as an accounting property rather than a feature - a double-entry ledger with the bank as a source of raw records - so it cannot be truthfully copied by a competitor that only copies the UI. Also records the raw-record immutability guarantee, the integer-minor-units money rule and the zero-telemetry/offline property as product constraints, and the monthly import-then-review rhythm with month-in-month read-only use. TWO OF THE BEAD'S THREE SUGGESTED REFUSALS WERE WRONG AND WERE CORRECTED BY ASKING. Cloud sync is wanted eventually, not refused. Automatic categorisation is acceptable provided the user can override it and create custom categories. What is genuinely refused is multi-user sharing and permissions. Those now sit under 'explicitly undecided' rather than being recorded as principles, because recording an unbuilt feature as a refusal would mislead every future round that reads it. The Evidence section states the absences future work must not fabricate: one user, no testimonials, no performance claims, no seed dataset, and an empty database holding three card statements with no checking or savings history - so chart work is not designed against an assumed populated ledger. title: M7: Rabobank + Revolut PDF importers (no provider id; Tier 3 only)
description:
CREATED 2026-10-03 during M1 bead cleanup, because renumbering the Amex PDF importer from M7 to M2 left the roadmap's actual M7 with no bead.

Roadmap position: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 --
  M7 | Rabobank + Revolut PDF importers | Itemized statement import; no provider ID ->
      Tier 3 only; per-account-type balance identity holds at delta 0

WHY THESE TWO ARE TOGETHER: both are PDF statement paths with NO usable provider transaction id,
so both are Tier 3 (content fingerprint) only. Neither can ever use Tier 1.

  Rabobank: the End-to-End ID is unusable as a dedup key (docs/research/11-real-export-
  verification.md section 3.4). It is in the data but must not be trusted as an identifier.
  Revolut: its stable 'id' was a CSV CLAIM and is UNVERIFIED (section 7). Do not build on it.
  Both provider enum values are DECLARED BUT NOT UPLOADABLE -- there is no FileAdapter for
  either. See docs/adr/0002-import-provider-enum.md.

THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THE HARD PART, and it is a REQUIRED test for every adapter:
the per-account-type balance identity must reconcile at DELTA 0 against the totals the statement
prints on its own front page. Account type is the discriminator and there is no generic form,
because the two directions are opposites:
    checking / savings (asset):  prev + credits - debits = closing
    credit_card (liability):     Vorig + Debiteringen - Crediteringen = Nieuw saldo
                                 -- a CHARGE INCREASES the amount owed
This identity caught every parsing bug during real-export verification, which is why it is
required rather than nice-to-have. It is deliberately NOT an invariants.yaml entry: the
right-hand side lives in the uploaded statement, not in the repo, and none of the checker's
three kinds (forbid_regex, hash, manifest) can execute a parse. An entry no checker can evaluate
always 'passes', which is worse than no entry -- it reads as coverage and is not coverage.
Rationale and rejected alternatives: docs/adr/0003-import-decisions-real-export.md Decision 2.

KNOWN PER-ADAPTER TRAPS (already diagnosed; do not re-derive):
- Revolut: one file can cover TWO accounts (Current + Deposit, with two own IBANs and no way to
  tell which row belongs to which). Rows whose ownership is ambiguous are HELD for explicit user
  confirmation and NOT written under a guessed account_id.
  docs/adr/0003-import-decisions-real-export.md Decision 4.
- Rabobank: type codes decide the sign, and a merchant-name rule must be LEARNED the same way.
  docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROPOSAL.md section H / ARCH:626.
- One file may therefore produce SEVERAL import_batch rows sharing one source_checksum, each with
  its own account_id. source_record.account_id is authoritative per row; import_batch.account_id
  is nullable and is NOT the row's account.

BLOCKING: needs the M2 persistence pipeline first (LifeOS-12). A parser alone does nothing --
M1 proved this: nothing writes parsed adapter records to the ledger yet.

Depends on: LifeOS-12 (M2).
close_reason: Done and verified against real statements (commit e2cfc77). rabobank_pdf.py and revolut_pdf.py exist, and the acceptance test this bead called 'the hard part' is implemented: backend/finance/tests/integration/test_real_statement_reconciliation.py reconciles both providers to delta 0 against the totals each statement prints on itself, using the per-account-type identity this bead specified. Rabobank is additionally chained across 4 consecutive months (each closing balance is the next opening). Sabotage cases prove the assertions can fail. 22 passed, 1 xfailed.

title: Populate exchange_rate so foreign-currency transactions can post
description:
BACKLOGGED BY OWNER 2026-10-03 during M1 (bead LifeOS-6). Not blocked on a decision -- blocked on data.

CURRENT STATE
- Schema is ready: finance.exchange_rate exists with
  UNIQUE (date, base_currency, quote_currency), base always EUR, and the column
  is 'units of quote per 1 EUR' (EUR 1 buys 160 JPY). source defaults to 'ecb'.
- It is EMPTY. No importer writes to it.
- Consequence: a manual transaction in any currency other than EUR is REFUSED
  with a 422 whose message says so plainly. EUR itself needs no row.

THE POLICY, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUG
backend/finance/api/routes/transactions.py:_base_rate looks up the EXACT booked
date and refuses when there is no row. It deliberately does NOT walk backwards to
a nearest prior rate. Reason: guessing which rate a date inherits writes a number
into the ledger that is not the true rate for that day, and it does so silently --
six months later nothing distinguishes an estimated row from a real one. Refusing
is the honest default.

Confirmed with the owner on 2026-10-03: keep refusing. Do not add a fallback
without a separate decision.

NOTE ON WHY THIS IS LOW PRIORITY RIGHT NOW
A nearest-prior fallback would NOT unblock anything today: the table is empty, so
there is no earlier rate to fall back TO either. Under either policy, zero
foreign-currency transactions can be entered until the table has rows. So the real
work is loading data, not changing the policy.

WHEN THIS BECOMES URGENT
The first Amex USD transaction. USD is an explicit v1 provider
(docs/adr/0002-import-provider-enum.md) and the Amex statement carries foreign
currency, so M2/M7 ingestion hits this before the ledger can hold an Amex row in
USD.

WORK
1. Load ECB daily reference rates into exchange_rate (date, 'EUR', quote, rate).
   The ECB publishes on business days only.
2. Decide how non-business-day dates are handled. This is the real question, and
   the one the current policy is silently deferring: a Saturday transaction has
   no rate of its own. Options: store the most recent business day's rate under
   the weekend date (explicitly an approximation), or have importers normalise a
   weekend transaction's VALUE_DATE to the preceding business day while keeping
   its posted date. The second keeps stored rates truthful; the first is simpler.
3. Until then, non-EUR manual posting refuses by design, and the error says why.
notes: PRODUCT CONTEXT (2026-10-05). The owner confirmed savings and investment tracking is wanted after V1. That makes this bead a prerequisite for the investments goal rather than a loose end: foreign-currency transactions cannot post until exchange_rate is populated, and investment holdings are denominated in things that are not EUR. Kept at p3 deliberately - V1 is spending.

title: Harden schema ownership with per-schema non-superuser DDL roles
description: LifeOS-ceu enforces no_cross_schema_fk with a ddl_command_end event trigger, which binds the superuser the app actually runs as but can itself be dropped by a superuser. The stronger boundary is per-schema non-superuser DDL roles (a role that owns finance and cannot REFERENCES core's tables), so a bad migration fails at the privilege layer rather than only at the trigger. That requires running each schema's migrations as its owner and would refactor the Makefile migrate target, backend/conftest.py _run_migrations, and both alembic/env.py files. Not needed for a single-user app with one superuser operator; revisit if a second operator or a non-superuser application role is introduced. Documented as a future option in docs/adr/0005-schema-ownership.md.

title: Privilege layer: reject identical-value writes to source_record
description:
BACKLOGGED BY OWNER 2026-10-03 during M1 (bead LifeOS-6). Explicitly deferred, with the owner agreeing the current behaviour is acceptable.

THE GAP, PRECISELY
raw_data_immutable is enforced by a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE row trigger
(finance.assert_source_record_raw_immutable). It rejects any write that CHANGES
raw_data or raw_description. It cannot reject this:

    UPDATE source_record SET raw_data = raw_data;   -- sets it to what it already was

Verified during M1: this statement passes. A Postgres row trigger sees the old row
and the new row; in that statement they are byte-identical, so there is nothing to
distinguish 'overwrote the evidence' from 'wrote the same evidence'. The trigger is
not weak here -- the information is not available to it.

SO THE GUARANTEE IS PRECISELY 'raw data never CHANGES', not 'raw data is never
WRITTEN'.

WHY THIS IS ACCEPTABLE FOR NOW (owner's judgement, 2026-10-03)
1. A same-value write mutates nothing. The stored evidence remains exactly what
   was imported.
2. Every actual tamper is blocked, including from a superuser.
3. The full fix requires a second database role:
       REVOKE UPDATE ON source_record FROM lifeos_app;
       GRANT UPDATE (status, journal_entry_id, error_message, occurrence_index)
         ON source_record TO lifeos_app;
   which means changing how the app connects, plus docker-compose and deployment.
   That is a deployment change for zero practical gain in a single-user app where
   one person controls all the code.

TRAP IF THIS IS EVER DONE -- verified during M1
'REVOKE UPDATE (raw_data, raw_description) ON source_record' ALONE IS A SILENT
NO-OP while the role still holds table-level UPDATE. information_schema still
reports UPDATE on raw_data after the column revoke, and the write goes through.
The table-level REVOKE is mandatory and must come first. A migration that appears
to add this protection but does not is worse than not adding it, because it reads
as coverage.

OPERATIONAL HAZARD OF THE FULL FIX
Because the GRANT enumerates permitted columns, any column added later without
updating it silently becomes un-updatable. That fails loudly (permission denied),
which is the right direction, but it is a maintenance coupling that belongs in a
comment in the migration when this is implemented.

REVISE THIS BEAD IF: the app ever gains a second user, or any non-trusted code
path is ever given write access to the database.

Related: docs/adr/0006-balance-trigger-and-db-invariants.md, which records why
M1 shipped the trigger rather than the privilege layer.
